clue.text: Insect surfacing under river, one that has gone through wood?

definitions.note: read with 'one' before it, the phrase is a noun: one that has gone through wood

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up to the surface means reading the word from bottom to top

blocks.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
the Roman numeral for one
a stinging insect

explanation.surface: A bug emerges beneath a river after boring its way through timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' does double duty: it gives I and also starts the definition, one that has gone through wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A ripsaw is a coarse saw for cutting timber along the grain, so it is a tool that has passed through wood.

clue.text: Tarantino maybe in uncovered vessel

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside its letters

blocks.note: bare means uncovered
Quentin is the first name of the film director Tarantino; 'maybe' marks him as one example of a Quentin

explanation.surface: The film director turns up aboard an open boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A barquentine is a three-masted sailing ship, square-rigged on the foremast only, so a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Little kids disturbing us most

indicators.note: disturbing things throws them out of their settled order

blocks.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: Small children bother us more than anything.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots, a smout is a small child or a little person, the same word as smolt, a young salmon.

clue.text: Cried, being cut off, hiding desire

indicators.note: to hide something is to hold it out of sight within

blocks.note: to shred is an old sense of to lop or cut off
an itch is a restless desire

explanation.surface: Someone wept at being cut off while concealing a longing.
explanation.definitionFit: Shritch is an old verb meaning to shriek or screech, so shritched is a past-tense word for cried out.

clue.text: The fellow with energy and vigour pushing up

blocks.note: the pronoun for a man
E is the physics symbol for energy
zing is liveliness or vigour

explanation.surface: A man full of energy and vigour pushes upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Heeze is a Scots verb meaning to hoist or raise, so heezing is lifting things up.

clue.text: Once sounded immoral, ditching wife

indicators.note: ditching something means getting rid of it, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: wrong means immoral
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: Something that once seemed wicked has been dumped along with a spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks an obsolete form: rong was an old past tense of ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Rong is an archaic past tense of ring, so it once meant rang, a bell having sounded.

clue.text: Cases from America brought into Asian country

indicators.note: something brought into a place ends up inside it

blocks.note: a country in southern Asia
abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: Crates shipped from the United States arrive in an Asian nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Indusia, plural of indusium, are membranous coverings, such as those over a fern's spore clusters: protective cases.

clue.text: What's left in vehicle — extra-large cigars

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside its letters

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
L is the abbreviation for left
OS stands for outsize, an extra-large clothing size

explanation.surface: Whatever remains in the car is a supply of big cigars.
explanation.definitionFit: A claro is a mild, light-coloured cigar, so claros are cigars of that kind.

clue.text: Soldier being grabbed by the female, a famous escape

indicators.note: something grabbed is held in the grip of what seizes it

blocks.note: the pronoun for a woman
GI is an American soldier
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier is seized by a woman and makes a celebrated getaway.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hegira was Muhammad's flight from Mecca to Medina in 622, the most famous escape in Islamic history.

clue.text: See mother outside biblical city with husband

indicators.note: a thing outside others wraps around them

blocks.note: a dam is an animal's mother
Ur of the Chaldees, Abraham's birthplace in Genesis
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Look: a mother stands outside an ancient city of the Bible with her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like an instruction to look, but it is the noun: a bishop's diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: Durham is the seat of one of England's senior bishops, so it is an episcopal see.

clue.text: One young creature hiding head and foot

indicators.note: with its head concealed, a word loses its first letter

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
a lamb is a young sheep

explanation.surface: A young animal tucks away its head and a foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot' belongs with the animal's body in the surface; it is the metrical foot.
explanation.definitionFit: An iamb is a metrical foot of one unstressed syllable followed by a stressed one.

clue.text: Flower that's small and delicate, not strong, knocked over

indicators.note: strong is forte in music, so its abbreviation is to be taken away
something knocked over ends up lying the other way round

blocks.note: elfin means small and delicate
F stands for forte, loud or strong in music

explanation.surface: A dainty, fragile bloom gets knocked down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is the crossword's river, something that flows, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower in crosswords is anything that flows, so a river such as the great African one qualifies.

clue.text: Prudent fellow is easily being seen as such

blocks.clueFragment: Prudent fellow is easily being seen as such
blocks.note: surface reading: a sensible man is readily recognised as sensible
setter's reading: the letters of 'is' sit plainly at the heart of the word for prudent, so that word is literally 'hearted' with is

explanation.surface: A sensible man is readily recognised as sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: WISE has IS at its heart, so it is IS-hearted, giving WISE-HEARTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Wise-hearted is an old word, used in the King James Bible, for someone who is wise and prudent in understanding.

clue.text: Lean going back to stop extremity falling over?

blocks.note: to prop something is to support it, stopping it from falling over
an end is an extremity
surface padding that rounds out the sense of the support

explanation.surface: Someone leans backwards to keep a tip from toppling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falling over?' fills out the sense of the support: a prop stops a thing falling over.
explanation.definitionFit: Propend is an archaic verb meaning to incline or be disposed towards, so it means to lean.

clue.text: Car used by Irish to get government revenues

blocks.note: Jag is a short name for a Jaguar car
IR is the abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: A car is driven by an Irishman to collect state income.
explanation.definitionFit: In India a jagir was a grant of land together with the government revenues it produced.

clue.text: Quick look from son facing set of questions

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
a quiz is a set of questions

explanation.surface: A boy facing a test gives the paper a brief glance.
explanation.definitionFit: Squiz is Australian and New Zealand slang for a quick glance or peek.

clue.text: Heal as before, given movement of air in violent flow

indicators.note: movement suggests letters shifting about into new positions
one thing placed in another sits inside its letters

blocks.note: a gush is a sudden violent outpouring
the letters as written

explanation.surface: Old-style healing calls for a draught of air in a strong stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As before' tells you the word is obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Guarish is an obsolete verb, from Old French, meaning to cure or heal.

clue.text: Certain root vegetables may be coarse, I do suspect

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters cannot be trusted as they stand

blocks.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: Someone suspects certain root vegetables are rough in texture.
explanation.definitionFit: Dioscorea is the genus of yams, whose starchy tubers are eaten as root vegetables.

clue.text: Throat no longer functioning? We had to engage hospital

indicators.note: to engage is to take on or hold, so one part is gripped inside another

blocks.note: we had is shortened to we'd
a san is a sanatorium

explanation.surface: A doctor's question about a dead throat, and we had to admit someone to hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer functioning' looks medical but flags an obsolete spelling: the usual form is weasand.
explanation.definitionFit: Wesand is an old spelling of weasand, the throat or windpipe, a word now out of use.

clue.text: Heretics with strange code cracked by Greek character

indicators.note: strange means odd or unusual, so the letters come out in an unexpected order
something cracked open lets another piece get inside it

blocks.note: the letters as written
eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Dissenters use an odd cipher that a Greek is able to crack.
explanation.definitionFit: The Docetae were early Christian heretics who held that Christ's body was only an appearance.

clue.text: With chemical lassie keeps performing

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold on to it inside

blocks.note: quine is a Scots word for a girl or lass
a performer is on, on stage

explanation.surface: A girl with a chemistry set carries on doing her act.
explanation.definitionFit: Quinone is an organic compound derived from benzene, used in dyes and photography, so a chemical.

clue.text: Old offices for example being set up to accommodate soldiers

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised, so the word reads upwards
accommodating someone means giving them room inside

blocks.note: say introduces an example, like e.g.
the men are the ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Former offices, for instance, are being fitted out to house troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A yamen was the office or residence of a Chinese mandarin under the empire, so these are old official offices.

clue.text: Change of utterance from second Indian leader not good

indicators.note: not means without, so the abbreviation for good is to be removed

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
Mahatma Gandhi led India's independence movement
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A change of tone comes from the second Indian leader, who was not much good.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandhi is the linguist's term for sound changes where words meet in speech, as in Sanskrit.

clue.text: Great excitement, not half — getting to eat and drink

indicators.note: not half means only half is kept and the rest is discarded

blocks.note: an orgasm is a climax of great excitement
taken as written

explanation.surface: Huge excitement, only halfway, about getting food and drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Orgeat is a sweet syrup flavoured with almonds, mixed into cocktails and cold drinks.

clue.text: Yesteryear's escapade with helpful woman meeting Her Majesty

blocks.note: an agony aunt helps readers with their troubles
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: An old adventure in which a kindly woman gets to meet the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Aunter is an obsolete word for an adventure, a daring exploit or escapade.

clue.text: Ring when there's something wrong, needing engineers in

indicators.note: a thing that needs something lacks it inside, so here it takes it in

blocks.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Call when there is a fault and engineers must come in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a phone call; it is a noun, the metal ring on a harness.
explanation.definitionFit: A torret is a variant of terret, one of the rings on a harness through which the reins pass.

clue.text: Liable to stop suddenly in freestyle

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the following word

blocks.note: letters two to seven of the word

explanation.surface: A swimmer doing front crawl tends to pull up without warning.
explanation.definitionFit: Reesty is a Scots word for restive or balky, said of a horse that refuses to go on.

clue.text: Artist in a scheme to acquire drug

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside its letters

blocks.note: taken as written
a tactic is a plan or scheme
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter is caught up in a plot to obtain narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: An ataractic is a tranquillising drug, one that produces calm.

clue.text: Mixed message about former No 1 LibDem?

blocks.note: Ming was the nickname of Sir Menzies Campbell, once Liberal Democrat leader
a former number one led

explanation.surface: A confusing statement concerning someone who used to lead the Liberal Democrats.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liberal Democrats are a British political party; 'Ming' Campbell was its leader in 2006-07, so Ming led.
explanation.definitionFit: Mingled means combined or blended together, a past-tense synonym of mixed.

clue.text: Beetle in window putting me off

indicators.note: putting something off here means sending it away, so the speaker's own pronoun is dropped

blocks.note: a dormer is a window set in a sloping roof

explanation.surface: A bug on the window pane is putting me off.
explanation.definitionFit: A dorr, or dor, is a dung beetle that flies with a loud droning hum.

clue.text: Short commission to the west not so far away once

indicators.note: something cut short loses its final letter
in an across clue, heading west means reading right to left

blocks.note: an errand is a task one is commissioned to do

explanation.surface: A brief assignment out west, which is nearer than it once was.
explanation.definitionFit: Narre is Spenser's form of nearer, meaning closer, so it is an old word for less distant.

clue.text: Old-fashioned supply to stop — you and I taken aback

indicators.note: taken aback suggests being pushed backwards, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: to end is to stop
you and I together are we

explanation.surface: An outdated stock is to be discontinued, and we are startled.
explanation.definitionFit: Endew is a Spenserian form of endue, to endow or furnish, so an old word for supply.

clue.text: Trees in Oz start to wither, probed by two holes

indicators.note: withering shrivels and distorts a thing, so the letters lose their shape
something probed has another thing pushed into it

blocks.note: the letters as written
each O is shaped like a hole

explanation.surface: Australian trees begin to droop, with a couple of holes bored into them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' reads as begin; here it is simply the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Tooart, or tuart, is a eucalyptus of Western Australia, so tooarts are trees in Australia.

clue.text: A bit of a laugh with spirit in aggressive dance?

blocks.note: ha is one burst of laughter
the ka is the soul or spirit in ancient Egyptian belief

explanation.surface: There's some fun with high spirits in a combative dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The haka is the Maori war dance, performed fiercely by New Zealand rugby teams before matches.

clue.text: Quaint, first to last — and drippy maybe

indicators.note: the opening letter is sent round to the end of the word

blocks.note: twee means quaint or cutesy

explanation.surface: Something cute moves from front to back and is a little soppy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drippy' sounds like feeble here, but it is meant literally: wet enough to drip.
explanation.definitionFit: Weet is a Scots and dialect form of wet, and something dripping is wet.

clue.text: Society languished, having shown indecision north of the border

definitions.text: shown indecision north of the border

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for society
to wither is to languish or fade

explanation.surface: High society faded away after dithering in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North of the border' means in Scotland, Scots being the source of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To swither is Scots for to hesitate or dither, so swithered means wavered between choices.
